fields.summary: Autonomous plan run for the bug that ship-change hands a whole change set back to the conductor when its merge finds origin/main moved or GitHub reports the PR conflicting. No owner took part. Research: internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml routes the merge step (rhiza ship check --no-rebase && rhiza ship merge) to handback:conduct on every fail, and wait-ci passes --no-rebase so a conflicting PR is never merged with main there; the conductor then runs rhiza ship rebase --no-push and goes through gate, signoff, push and CI again. rhiza ship rebase (internal/api/ship_rebase.go) already merges origin/main, settles rendered-only conflicts, runs the local gate and pre-push check and pushes, leaving a code conflict in progress (exit 1) and a merged head the gate failed on unpushed (exit 1); rhiza ship check --settled without --no-rebase already merges main on a conflicting PR the same way (shipSettleConflict) and keeps waiting on the pushed head. plan.toml's merge step already fails to a rebase step that loops back through a CI wait (max_visits 6). Plan: wait-ci drops --no-rebase; the merge step is split into pr-green (rhiza ship check, fail hands back) and merge (rhiza ship merge, fail goes to a new rebase step running rhiza ship rebase that passes back to wait-ci and hands back on fail: a code conflict left in progress, or the local gate or pre-push check failing on the merged head); the conduct prompt, the conduct-handback and conduct-roles topics, the workflows topic, docs/primitives.md and the ship-change-one-ci script follow. rhiza ship rebase --no-push stays as a flag. Not breaking, not severe.
fields.title: Plan: ship steps rebase a clean merge of main (autonomous plan run)
